effective_date_basis: The 'until' date in the order's text; for an event-relative date (the exemplar: sixty days after the convening of the second session of the 73rd Congress) the agent computes it from a cited source for the event and states the computation; or the date of the next extension if earlier.
ending_pattern: The order continues a body or extends a time limit or effective date until a stated or computable date. It ends on that date unless extended or replaced by a later order issued before expiry (which amends the date; it is not a revocation). When a deferral order expires, the deferred measure takes effect or is deferred again: that is the other order's event, not an end of this order's subject.

exceptions_savings.assessment: Acts done under the extension are accrued effects.

exemplar.wpa_summary: Effectivedates for the abolitionof the Federal Employ ment StabilizationBoard deferred until 60 days after the convening of the 2d sessionof the 73d Congress.

legal_effect: Research pattern only. A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order, and never substitutes for reading the order's own text.
outlier_conditions: The order's own text (not only the WPA summary or APP title) does not match the type, or the held text is another order's.
The order does more than the type's single act (a second operative clause of another kind).
A later order or statute amends, extends, revokes or revives it before the candidate end.
The order states its own effective date, duration, condition or termination that differs from the pattern.
The deferred measure was later rescinded, so the deferral never matured.
quoted_clause:
6166, relating
to co-operative vocational education and rehabilitation, payments for agricultural
experiment stations, co-operative agricultural extension work, and endowment and
maintenance of colleges for the benefit of agriculture and the mechanic arts, and the
effective date for the abolishment of the Federal Employment Stabilization Board
and the transfer of its records to the Federal Emergency Administration of Public
Works, as provided in the last paragraph of Section 1 of said Executive Order, are
hereby deferred until sixty days after the convening of the second session of the 73rd
Congress.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT.

Tue Waits Hovsz,

July 26, 1933.

[No. 6221]
